# core/fs

`core/fs` — paths and directories: join, dirname, a recursive mkdir and
fresh temporary directories. Paths are `/`-separated strings.

Generated from [src/core/fs.ts](https://github.com/amritk/vector/blob/main/src/core/fs.ts).

## Declarations

### joinPath

Joins two path parts with one `/` between them. An absolute `b` replaces `a`,
and an empty part is dropped.

```ts
function joinPath(a: string, b: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="a" type="string" required>

the leading part

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="string" required>

the trailing part

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the joined path

</scalar-field>

### dirname

The directory part of a path, as POSIX `dirname` answers it: "." for a bare
name and "/" for a file at the root.

```ts
function dirname(path: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

the path to cut

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

everything before the last `/`, without trailing slashes

</scalar-field>

### basename

The last part of a path, as POSIX `basename` answers it: trailing slashes
are dropped, and a path of only slashes is "/". An empty path gives "".

```ts
function basename(path: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

the path to cut

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

everything after the last `/`

</scalar-field>

### relativePath

The path that leads from directory `from` to `to`, as a relative import
spells it: starting `./` or `../`. Both must be absolute and free of `..`
parts, as `realpathSync` answers them; nothing on disk is read.

```ts
function relativePath(from: string, to: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="from" type="string" required>

the directory to start from

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="to" type="string" required>

the path to reach

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

`./<path>` when `to` is at or below `from`, else `../` once per
  part of `from` to climb, then the rest of `to`

</scalar-field>

### mkdirAll

Makes a directory and every missing parent, like `mkdir -p`.

```ts
function mkdirAll(path: string, mode: i32): Result<boolean, string>
```

<scalar-field name="path" type="string" required>

the directory to make

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="mode" type="i32" required>

the permission bits for each directory it makes

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;boolean, string&gt;">

`Ok(true)` when the directory exists afterwards, or `Err` naming
  the part that could not be made

</scalar-field>

### makeTempDir

Makes a new, empty directory only the current user can read, under
`$TMPDIR` (or `/tmp`), with a random name that starts with `prefix`.

```ts
function makeTempDir(prefix: string): Result<string, string>
```

<scalar-field name="prefix" type="string" required>

the start of the directory's name, such as "vector-"

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Result&lt;string, string&gt;">

`Ok` with the directory's path, or `Err` when none could be made

</scalar-field>
